name: metashell
why: An interactive shell for stepping through C++ template metaprogramming, opening a strange window onto compile-time computation.

brief.what_it_is: Metashell is an interactive shell for C++ template metaprogramming, in the spirit of the Python, Haskell (ghci) and Erlang shells. You type template metaprograms at a prompt and it evaluates them using Clang, so you can see the result of a compile-time computation without writing a source file and wrestling the compiler into printing it. The Homebrew formula installs a large LLVM/Clang toolchain alongside it, including a metashell executable and a templight tool family.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage argues that beginners in C++ template metaprogramming have to learn tricks to make a compiler reveal the result of simple metaprograms, and that debugging metaprograms is hard because compilers are not built to expose intermediate results. Metashell is meant to make that easier with a REPL, as other languages have.
brief.how_it_works: The README says only that Metashell 'uses Clang to evaluate the metaprograms'. The executables list shows a metashell binary and templight, templight++, templight-cl and templight_metashell alongside a full set of Clang and LLVM tools, which suggests a Clang-based backend bundled with the shell. I did not find a more detailed mechanism description in the pages I read.

commands_seen.context: Homebrew install line on the binary installers page under OS X; the only install command shown.

brief.install_notes: Official binaries exist for Ubuntu 18.04, Debian 9.5, Fedora 28, OpenSuSE Leap 42.2 and Windows (version 4.0.0). On OS X the installers page says to install with Homebrew and that Xcode with the Command Line Developer Tools must be installed for Metashell to work properly. Older versions (3.0.0, 2.x, 1.0.0) have installers for older distributions. Building from source is also an option, per the installers page, but I did not read build steps. The README links to an online demo at metashell.org/about/demo.
brief.standout: It is a REPL for C++ template metaprogramming, which is an unusual niche: the compiler is driven interactively to evaluate metafunctions and show their results. The Homebrew formula pulls in a complete LLVM/Clang distribution with it, which makes the install large.
brief.status: Quiet, with mixed signals. The README's latest installer is version 4.0.0, and the newest distributions named there (Ubuntu 18.04, Debian 9.5, Fedora 28) are from around 2018. The README build badges point to travis-ci.org and AppVeyor, and the Travis service was retired, so the CI links are probably stale. I could not see a last-release or last-commit date in the pages I fetched, so the exact date is unknown.
brief.caveats: The OS X note says Xcode with Command Line Developer Tools is required. The installers page lists only older Linux distributions, so current versions of Ubuntu, Debian and Fedora may need a source build. The README's CI badges point to Travis, which is probably no longer running. The Homebrew formula's executables list is very large, so the shell is a small part of a big toolchain install. The GPLv3 license applies.
quotes: The goal of this project is to provide an interactive template metaprogramming shell.
Metashell provides an interactive shell similar to the Python, Haskell and Erlang shells for template metaprogramming. It uses Clang to evaluate the metaprograms.
Metashell is published under the GNU General Public License, version 3.
